results.title: Bringing Interdisciplinary Data Science Education ...
results.content: To sum up, IDSE refers to the theory and practice of teaching and learning as it applies to: (a) data science and related classrooms that are increasingly demanded by both employers and educators, which (b) transcend simple numerical proficiency, programming, or coding, and (c) share the following commonalities: they are interdisciplinary by nature and are taught at various STEM, social sciences, and increasingly humanities departments; they use data as a fundamental component; and they rely on computational techniques to explore and illuminate specific phenomena. We then dive into four interdependent challenges: (a) the complexity of interdisciplinarity; (b) the varied skills in the interdisciplinary classroom—a common issue in all classrooms whatever the subject or level, but particularly relevant in data science; (c) decolonization in a methodological and data-driven context; and (d) the challenge of teaching ethics in an era where data increasingly shapes human existence.
